# VoiceDebrief

> Drop in a voice note or an audio recording (.opus / .ogg / .m4a / .mp3 / .wav /
> .aac / .flac) and get back a transcript, an optional translation, a written
> debrief and — if asked — an infographic, in one pass. WhatsApp is one of several
> ways audio arrives here, not the product. Everything runs in the browser with the
> user's own OpenRouter key: there is no backend of ours and no account system, so
> nothing is uploaded to us or stored server-side. The audio IS sent to OpenRouter
> and on to a model provider we neither choose nor know — see the privacy section
> on the landing page before uploading anything sensitive. In beta. We charge
> nothing and add no margin; the key holder pays OpenRouter directly, typically
> well under £0.01 per pass, with a declared maximum shown before each run. Built
> in the open by an agentic team; every claim on this site links to its source in
> the public repository.

The app is a JavaScript tool published as `window.__tool` (an SgToolApi named
`whatsapp-transcribe`). If you are an agent operating the app or explaining it,
the machine-readable surfaces below are maintained for you and are always in
step with the deployed build.

The same is true of everything under `/tools/`: each is a single-purpose page
that publishes its own `window.__tool`, with a manifest and a skills document,
so an agent can do what a person does there without a UI.

## The app, for agents

- [API skill](https://voicedebrief.ai/app/skills/SKILL__api.md): every `window.__tool` action with params and returns — run a pass, read results, drive the chat, read the workflow and its execution trace
- [Browser-use skill](https://voicedebrief.ai/app/skills/SKILL__browser.md): operating the app through its UI
- [Human guide](https://voicedebrief.ai/app/skills/SKILL__human.md): the app explained for people
- [Action manifest](https://voicedebrief.ai/app/manifest.json): the full action list, machine-readable
- [The declared workflow](https://voicedebrief.ai/app/workflows/standard.json): the one-pass as a JSON state machine — steps, models, per-step spending ceilings, transitions, failure behaviour. The app executes from this file

## The tools, for agents

- [Tools](https://voicedebrief.ai/tools/): the index — small, single-purpose browser tools built alongside the app
- [Extract audio from a video](https://voicedebrief.ai/tools/extract-audio/): a video in, its soundtrack out as `.m4a`, entirely in the browser via FFmpeg WASM — no upload, no key, no cost. `-vn -c:a copy` where the audio is AAC; automatic AAC re-encode where it cannot be copied (Opus in WebM), reported as `reencoded: true`. The first extraction fetches ~32 MB of FFmpeg core from unpkg.com, on demand
- [Extract audio — API skill](https://voicedebrief.ai/tools/extract-audio/skills/SKILL__api.md): `extractAudio`, `prepare`, `isSupported`, `probe`, `getLastAudio`, `saveLastAudio`, `sendToApp`. Audio is opt-in (`withAudio: true`) because a soundtrack is large. Same synchronous `window.__tool` publication as the other tools
- [Extract audio — action manifest](https://voicedebrief.ai/tools/extract-audio/manifest.json)
- [Text to speech](https://voicedebrief.ai/tools/text-to-speech/): text in, a spoken `.wav` out, in the browser on the caller's own OpenRouter key
- [Text to speech — API skill](https://voicedebrief.ai/tools/text-to-speech/skills/SKILL__api.md): every action with params, returns, typed errors and a Playwright example. `window.__tool` is assigned while the page's module evaluates — before load completes and without waiting on any network — and `window.__toolStatus` always states the mode and any engine error. Wait with `waitForFunction(() => window.__tool)`, not on `readyState`. Audio comes back as base64, because a Blob does not survive `page.evaluate`
- [Text to speech — human guide](https://voicedebrief.ai/tools/text-to-speech/skills/SKILL__human.md)
- [Text to speech — action manifest](https://voicedebrief.ai/tools/text-to-speech/manifest.json)

## Live state, machine-readable

- [status.json](https://voicedebrief.ai/engineering/status.json): the deployed version, commit, and the per-layer test results this deploy passed
- [issues.json](https://voicedebrief.ai/engineering/issues.json): the full issue queue (open/blocked/done) as of this deploy
- [docs.json](https://voicedebrief.ai/engineering/docs.json): the public documentation inventory
- [versions.json](https://voicedebrief.ai/versions/versions.json): every release with date, headline and changes
- [updates.json](https://voicedebrief.ai/updates/updates.json): every Updates post, structured
- [videos.json](https://voicedebrief.ai/videos/videos.json): the demo videos
- [RSS feed](https://voicedebrief.ai/updates/feed.xml)
- [guide.json](https://voicedebrief.ai/user-guide/guide.json): the user guide as data — each step with its test-captured screenshot
- [baseline-changes.json](https://voicedebrief.ai/user-guide/baseline-changes.json): every time the product's screenshots moved, tied to the commit and CI run that moved them (the agent-review surface for UI change)

## Pages

- [How it works, where the audio goes, what it costs](https://voicedebrief.ai/): the landing page — the tool runs on the page itself; the beta is bring-your-own-key and there is no plan, credit or card
- [Colour schemes](https://voicedebrief.ai/vd-tokens.css): five, switchable from the header and remembered per browser — Signal (light, default), Night, Paper, Blueprint, Ember. `data-vd-theme` on `<html>`; `window.__vdTheme` reads and sets it. The workbench pins itself to Signal while its older components are ported
- [The Workbench](https://voicedebrief.ai/app/): the working surface — the same one pass, plus chat with the debrief, the declared workflow and its trace, the raw OpenRouter calls, and prompt overrides. Still served from `/app/`: the address is not the name
- [Getting an OpenRouter key](https://voicedebrief.ai/openrouter-key/): why the product is bring-your-own-key, the five steps to create one, how to cap its spend, and how to revoke it. Nobody can use the product without this
- [User guide](https://voicedebrief.ai/user-guide/): step-by-step usage — every screenshot taken by a passing test on the same build
- [How the browser does the work](https://voicedebrief.ai/engineering/wasm/): WebAssembly in this product — FFmpeg compiled to WASM, running in the tab, on a video that is never uploaded. The nine-step sequence behind the extract-audio tool, the stream-copy-then-re-encode rule, what the design costs (a 32 MB core, single-threaded, a CDN inside the CSP) and the two failures it produced. Transcription is NOT local: that page says so as plainly as this one does
- [Engineering](https://voicedebrief.ai/engineering/): how it is built — pipeline, testing, docs, security posture (including open findings, honestly labelled), team, concepts
- [Concepts](https://voicedebrief.ai/engineering/concepts/): the concept scheme behind the interface vocabulary — meaning stored in a definition, one label per culture, and the English review that found three words naming the wrong thing. NOT wired to the shipped strings; it is a review surface
- [concepts.json](https://voicedebrief.ai/engineering/concepts/concepts.json): that scheme as data — definitions, scope notes, per-culture labels, verdicts and broader/narrower/related relations
- [Design candidates](https://voicedebrief.ai/design/): the A/B hub — three theme prototypes and four culture packs, each runnable with synthetic data and no key. Design references under evaluation, not the shipping product (noindex, absent from the sitemap)
- [Browser unit tests](https://voicedebrief.ai/tests/browser/): the app's unit suite, runnable in your browser against the deployed modules
- [Updates](https://voicedebrief.ai/updates/): the dated build-in-public record
- [Versions](https://voicedebrief.ai/versions/): every release, with diffs
- [Videos](https://voicedebrief.ai/videos/): demos and shorts
- [Tools](https://voicedebrief.ai/tools/): small browser tools built alongside the app — extracting audio from video, and text to speech
- [Library](https://voicedebrief.ai/library/): every document behind the product

## Source

- [Repository](https://github.com/sgraph-ai/SGraph-AI__SaaS__WhatsApp__Audio__Transcription): everything — code, briefs, decisions, reviews, this file
